evidence: Plan: "when `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` is an `io.TextIOWrapper` with a non-UTF-8 encoding, `reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")`": stdin is not mentioned

findings.finding: Forcing `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` to UTF-8 in `main` changes the byte contract for every external consumer of piped rebar CLI output, and it silently overrides an explicit `PYTHONIOENCODING`. The plan does not acknowledge either effect. Its 'no-op on Linux/macOS' claim also holds only for UTF-8 locales: an ISO-8859-1 locale (PEP 538/540 coercion applies only to C/POSIX) would be reconfigured too.
scenarios: Windows platform, .NET or Ruby target project: a non-Python harness (or PowerShell 5.1 with its default ANSI/OEM `[Console]::OutputEncoding`) pipes `rebar` output and decodes it with the code page. Before the change, a ticket title with `é` printed correctly in cp1252; after it, the user sees mojibake such as `Ã©`.
A user who deliberately sets `PYTHONIOENCODING` to match a downstream tool finds the setting ignored.
Linux developer workstation with a non-UTF-8 locale (e.g. `LANG=en_US.ISO-8859-1`): output switches from locale bytes to UTF-8, contrary to the plan's 'no-op on Linux/macOS' statement.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Note that piped CLI output on non-UTF-8 hosts becomes UTF-8 as an intended contract. Reword 'no-op on Linux/macOS' as 'no-op when the stream is already UTF-8'.

findings.finding: Reconfiguring `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` to UTF-8 changes the bytes rebar emits when output is piped on Windows. It also changes them on any Linux host with a non-UTF-8 locale, despite the claim that it is a 'no-op on Linux/macOS'. Downstream consumers that decode with the console or locale codec, such as PowerShell pipelines, will see different output. The plan does not acknowledge this behaviour change.
scenarios: A Windows user pipes `rebar ...` into a cp1252-decoding tool. Non-ASCII characters that previously round-tripped (e.g. `é`) now arrive as mojibake.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Keep each stream's existing error handler when reconfiguring: `stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors=stream.errors)`.
evidence: Plan: "`reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")`": no `errors=` argument
CPython TextIOWrapper.reconfigure: when encoding is given and errors is not, errors defaults to 'strict'
src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:318 `install_stderr_handler("rebar")` and :331-341 `sys.stderr.write(...)` depend on stderr never raising
findings.finding: `TextIOWrapper.reconfigure(encoding=...)` without `errors=` resets the error handler to 'strict'. `sys.stderr` normally uses 'backslashreplace' so diagnostics can never crash. The planned call therefore makes stderr strict, so a lone surrogate (for example a surrogateescape-decoded path) written to stderr would raise inside the logging handler or the error-rendering code in `main`, instead of being escaped.
scenarios: A diagnostic containing a surrogate-escaped filename goes to the reconfigured stderr on Windows → UnicodeEncodeError instead of an escaped message
findings.suggested_fix: `for s in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr): if isinstance(s, io.TextIOWrapper) and codecs.lookup(s.encoding).name != "utf-8": s.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors=s.errors)`

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Have `_read_existing_commit` read with `encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"` so a cp1252 stale file still gives its ASCII `COMMIT` SHA, and change the edge test to assert the SHA is preserved instead of 'no baked SHA'.
evidence: Plan: "`_read_existing_commit` (`:65`) treats `UnicodeDecodeError` as \"no baked SHA\""
hatch_build.py:9-20: precedence step 2 exists to 'PRESERVE an existing non-null COMMIT' on the rebuild-from-sdist path, which has no git or env
hatch_build.py:113-117: the only non-ASCII byte is in the docstring; the COMMIT line is an ASCII repr
findings.finding: Treating `UnicodeDecodeError` in `_read_existing_commit` as 'no baked SHA' throws away a commit that could still be recovered. In a cp1252 `_build_info.py`, only the docstring's em dash (0x97) is non-UTF-8; the `COMMIT = '<sha>'` line is pure ASCII. Reading with `errors="replace"` would still let `ast.parse` succeed and return the SHA. Returning None instead drops into `_build_commit`, which gives None in a rebuild-from-sdist tree with no `.git`. That brings back the 'COMMIT = None in the published wheel' failure this hook exists to prevent.
findings.location: Approach — `hatch_build.py` bullet (`_read_existing_commit` (`:65`)); Testing — 'a cp1252 stale `_build_info.py` yields no baked SHA'
scenarios: An sdist built by the pre-fix hook on Windows (cp1252 file) is rebuilt into a wheel with no `.git`: the wheel bakes `COMMIT = None` although the SHA was in the file
findings.suggested_fix: `text = target.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")`. Replacement characters only land in the docstring, so `ast.parse` succeeds and the existing literal-`COMMIT` extraction returns the SHA. The new edge test should write a cp1252 file with `COMMIT = 'abc1234'` and assert `'abc1234'` is returned.
